officialTitle: Atezolizumab and Nab-Paclitaxel in Advanced Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
setting: First-line unresectable locally advanced or metastatic

primaryEndpoints: OS (ITT; then PD-L1-positive subgroup if significant)
design.notes: 1:1 randomisation, 451 patients per group. Stratified by prior (neo)adjuvant taxane, liver metastases, and PD-L1 status. OS testing hierarchical: PD-L1-positive OS formally tested only if ITT OS significant.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding atezolizumab to nab-paclitaxel improve PFS and OS as first-line therapy for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, overall and in PD-L1-positive tumours?

pico.population: Untreated unresectable locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
pico.outcomes: Co-primary: PFS (ITT and PD-L1-positive) and OS (ITT, then PD-L1-positive)

publications.title: Atezolizumab and Nab-Paclitaxel in Advanced Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Each group included 451 patients (median follow-up, 12.9 months). In the intention-to-treat analysis, the median progression-free survival was 7.2 months with atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel, as compared with 5.5 months with placebo plus nab-paclitaxel (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.80; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.92; P=0.002)
among patients with PD-L1-positive tumors, the median progression-free survival was 7.5 months and 5.0 months, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.49 to 0.78; P<0.001)

In the intention-to-treat analysis, the median overall survival was 21.3 months with atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel and 17.6 months with placebo plus nab-paclitaxel (hazard ratio for death, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.02; P=0.08)
among patients with PD-L1-positive tumors, the median overall survival was 25.0 months and 15.5 months, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.86)

safety.description: Adverse events leading to discontinuation of any agent
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events that led to the discontinuation of any agent occurred in 15.9% of the patients who received atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel and in 8.2% of those who received placebo plus nab-paclitaxel.

limitations: ITT OS not statistically significant, so the PD-L1-positive OS result could not be formally tested under the hierarchy
Interim OS analysis at the time of the primary report

clinicalImplications.text: First phase III trial to show a PFS benefit from adding a PD-L1 inhibitor to chemotherapy in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, with benefit concentrated in PD-L1-positive tumours; the OS signal in that subgroup was not formally tested.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Read IMpassion130 alongside KEYNOTE-355: in both, PD-L1 status defined who benefited, but the assays and cutoffs differ and are not interchangeable.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 30345906. Later OS updates not ingested. Result classified MIXED because ITT PFS was positive but ITT OS was not significant.
